name: GPT Healthcare Ltd
tagline: Cost-efficient eastern-India hospital operator trading at a discount to peers, but growth is too moderate for the 10x/2-3yr bar
business_overview: GPT Healthcare runs multi-specialty hospitals concentrated in eastern India (Kolkata, Agartala, with expansion into Ranchi/Raipur), on a capital-light model of smaller 100-200 bed facilities versus peers' 300-400 bed hospitals. Average capex/bed ~Rs 5.2m, well below larger listed peers. Meaningful medical-tourism exposure (Bangladesh). Small, low-activity ValuePickr thread.
fundamentals_table: ~14% revenue CAGR; FY26 revenue ~Rs 1.32bn/quarter run-rate, Q2 FY26 saw profit slump / margin squeeze
fundamentals_narrative: Capital efficiency is genuinely good (ROCE ~23%, ROE ~16%) with a near-debt-free balance sheet and a low-capex expansion model that has a track record of EBITDA breakeven within a year for new hospitals. But revenue growth is a moderate ~14% CAGR and the most recent quarter (Q2 FY26) showed a profit slump and margin compression. The main re-rating angle is a ~40-50% valuation discount to larger listed hospital peers.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. 52-week range Rs 126-186; stock has been rangebound-to-soft.
sentiment_summary: Small ValuePickr thread (5 posts in stream, highest post #7), last activity October 2024 — effectively dormant. Read all inline posts. Original write-up (vx294, 15 loves) is a primer on hospital metrics + the eastern-India opportunity; AkshayThakur and Naman_Bhansali added notes on cost-efficient expansion and the peer valuation discount. No new forum activity since Oct 2024.
community_signal: No trusted-roster users in the thread. Highest-signal post: Naman_Bhansali (9 loves) framed GPT as a cost-effective, smaller-format operator at a ~40-50% valuation discount to industry, targeting low-bed-density tier-1/2 cities. Constructive but not a high-conviction call, and over a year stale.
bull_case: Strong capital efficiency (ROCE ~23%) and a proven low-capex, fast-breakeven expansion model
Near debt-free; disciplined balance sheet for a hospital operator
Trades at a material (~40-50%) valuation discount to larger listed hospital peers — a re-rating lever if growth holds
bear_case: ~14% revenue CAGR is far short of what a 10x-in-2-3-years outcome would require
Q2 FY26 profit slump and margin squeeze raise near-term execution questions
Regional concentration in West Bengal / eastern India; hospital capex cycles are lumpy
ValuePickr thread is dormant (last post Oct 2024) — no independent community validation of the current trajectory
verdict_headline: Good-quality regional hospital compounder, but the growth rate doesn't clear the open-screen 10x/2-3yr bar
verdict_reasoning: ROCE ~23% and a capital-light model are real positives, and a ~40-50% peer valuation discount gives a re-rating angle
But ~14% revenue CAGR plus a Q2 FY26 profit slump means this reads as a steady compounder, not a 2-3 year multi-bagger — thesis_fit 'neither'
Old 108-stock project rated this Tier A as a 'discovery candidate'; under the no-ceiling open-screen thesis it is 'neither' because the growth rate, not the quality, is the binding constraint

four_box.note: Verdict explicit: '~40-50% peer valuation discount gives a re-rating angle' (valuation=yes); but '~14% revenue CAGR plus a Q2 FY26 profit slump' reads as 'a steady compounder, not a 2-3 year multi-bagger' (tailwind weak).
